newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court annuls in part Commission decision on Tierce Ladbroke.
newsitem.headline: Court annuls in part Commission decision on Tierce Ladbroke.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance partially upheld on Thursday Tierce Ladbroke's attempt to force the European Commission to find restrictions against retransmissions of horse races illegal.

The court threw out allegations of inadequate reasoning by the Commission but did find the Commission failed to fully consider whether the horse racing associations contracted among themselves to prevent retransmission of races to Ladbroke.

The court annulled the part of the Commission decision which took the position that the horse racing associations did not contract among themselves to refuse retransmission of races in Belgium because none of the associations take bets on the betting market in Belgium. The court found "the Commission did not examine that part of the applicant's complaint with the required diligence."

Ladbroke alleged that refusals by Pari Mutuel Urbain and Pari Mutuel International, the principal French horse racing associations, to permit the restransmission abroad of horse races staged in Belgium violated Community competiton laws.
The Commission declined to take on Ladbroke's complaint after finding "insufficient grounds for finding of infringement," court documents said.
"Article 86 - Relevant market - Joint dominant position - Refusal to grant a trasmission licence - Article 85(1) - Clause prohibiting retransmission"

application for annulment of the Commission decision rejecting a complaint lodged by Tierce Ladbroke SA (IV/33.699) against the principal French societes de course (horse-racing associations), Pari Mutuel International, alleging infringement of articles 85 and 86 of the EEC treaty, and for an order requiring the Commission to re-examine that complaint forthwith

1. Annuls the Commission decision rejecting a complaint lodged by Tierce Ladbroke SA (IV/33.699) in so far as it considers that the refusal of the societes de course to grant the applicant a licence for the transmission of French races in Belgium, as notified to the applicant by a letter from Pari Mutuel Urbain dated 9 August 1990, was the normal consequence of the fact that neither Pari Mutuel Urbain nor the societes de course take bets on the betting market in Belgium, and therefore could not be the subject of an agreement between the societes de courses within the meaning of article 85(1) of the treaty;
2. Dismisses the remainder of the application;
3. Orders the parties, including the interveners, to bear their own costs.
